item.title: Sorry, haters. Ferrari’s first EV is doing just fine
item.dc:creator: Tim De Chant
item.description: To the horror of commenters across the internet, the Ferrari Luce appears to be a sales success.

item.title: Waymo robotaxis are starting to return to freeways
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec
item.description: Waymo robotaxis are now using freeways in Phoenix with more cities to follow in the coming days.

item.title: US government bans new foreign-made humanoids, robot dogs, and solar inverters, citing risks to national security
item.dc:creator: Zack Whittaker
item.description: The ban largely affects U.S. imports from China, which currently dominates the global market for making humanoid robots and solar inverters.

item.title: Google brings its age-assurance technology to Android developers worldwide
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Google is expanding its Play Age Signals API, giving Android developers a privacy-preserving way to tailor experiences based on users’ age ranges.

item.title: Elon Musk’s X settles multiyear legal battle with the World Federation of Advertisers
item.dc:creator: Aisha Malik
item.description: X sued the WFA in 2024 for conducting what it called a "systematic illegal boycott" of the platform after it saw a decline in advertising revenue following Musk's $44 billion takeover of the social network.

item.title: Hint, a new AI startup co-founded by Martha Stewart, offers an AI assistant for homeowners
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: AI home management startup Hint, co-founded by Martha Stewart, wants to become an “AI for your home,” combining property records, maintenance schedules, home documents, and an AI assistant into a single app.

item.title: Perplexity employee who worked on Comet launches an AI browser aimed at knowledge work
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: Polar has come out with an AI-first browser aimed at knowledge workers, and it has now raised a $5.7 million seed round led by Madrona.

item.title: Encore AI raises $30M to build AI agents that learn from customer calls
item.dc:creator: Ram Iyer
item.description: The startup analyzes calls, messages, and CRM data to identify effective sales techniques and turn them into playbooks for AI agents.

item.title: ‘No one’s making a phone like this’: Light’s co-founders on building for the anti-smartphone generation
item.dc:creator: Theresa Loconsolo
item.description: With the Light Phone, Kaiwei Tang and Joe Hollier have spent over a decade exploring the value of simplicity in our relationship to technology, partnering along the way with players like Andrew Yang, Kendrick Lamar, and Pete Davidson. Now, with a new flip phone and a growing wave of “attention activists” pushing back against Big Tech, they think the rest of […]

item.title: DoorDash is building its own drone delivery business
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec
item.description: DoorDash has received FAA approval to operate a commercial drone delivery service in the United States.

item.title: Fast Metals is treating waste with more waste to extract critical minerals
item.dc:creator: Tim De Chant
item.description: Aluminum production has saddled the world with billions of tons of caustic waste. One startup has a plan to clean it up and turn a profit.

item.title: As AI content floods the internet, Pangram raises $9M to detect it
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bellan
item.description: Pangram has raised $9 million to scale its AI detection software. The startup has also released a new AI text detection model, Pangram 4, and an AI image detection model in research preview.

item.title: Cyera agrees to acquire Oasis Security for $1B to safeguard proliferating AI agents
item.dc:creator: Marina Temkin
item.description: The deal is Cyera's third acquisition this year.

item.title: Bot-detection startup Spur nabs $200M from Insight
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: Spur Intelligence has raised a $200 million round from Insight Partners for its tech that can identify legit human traffic from bots.

item.title: MCP startup Runlayer accuses Rippling of stealing its product idea
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: Runlayer is suing Rippling after Rippling evaluated the startup's MCP gateway product and then opted to build one itself.

item.title: Sam Altman is ready to decelerate
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: His change of position comes after "the first security incident that I have felt very viscerally."

item.title: Ozlo’s Sleepbuds 2 build on Bose’s sleep earbud legacy
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Ozlo’s first major update to its sleep earbuds introduces longer battery life, improved connectivity, enhanced audio, and new sleep features as the startup continues the product line once abandoned by Bose.

item.title: The robot NASA hired to lift a orbital telescope tumbled out of control
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: According to NASA, two of the three reaction wheels that control the spacecraft's alignment have failed, and there are problems with one of the spacecraft's thruster systems.

item.title: Waymo, robotaxi operators face fresh scrutiny over emergency response failures
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec
item.description: Rep. Kevin Mullin (D-California ) has proposed a bill that would direct federal regulators to establish minimum national safety standards for autonomous vehicle operators.

item.title: eBay reaches $56M settlement with e-commerce newsletter writers it terrorized in 2019
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: Ina and David Steiner inspired the ire of high-level eBay executives after occasionally criticizing the company in their newsletter. In 2019, a plot was concocted to intimidate the couple into halting their negative coverage.
